posts.cooked: Any card with a "vaguely ambiguous" working has probably thus already been queried about on this forum (though whether the wording on a card is ambiguous is probably down to the opinion of whomever is reading said card at the time). Was there anything specific you wanted to ask about? Because that's partially what the forum is for (you know, apart from us all generally spouting off about how cool the game and >G are :D), after all ;).

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
Edwin:

I agree with all of that except the "pretty much every significant query".  He's not even close to that; every card whose workings are even vaguely ambiguous deserves to be clarified, and he only has a few of the earliest and most often-repeated questions.

That's not true.  To my knowledge, I have every single instance where a >G employee has laid down a ruling on a particular card or interaction.  Unless by "every significant query" you mean "every question ever asked (whether answered or not) including all possible future questions", I think I've got it covered.  And if I don't, just point me to one I've missed and I'll add it.  Easy peasy.

FWIW, I'm on Team Silverleaf.  Imagine an encyclopedia with no chapters or headings, with all the info jumbled together into a single gigantic entry.  That's what a forum that isn't well-groomed into separate threads for separate topics would become.

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
I would absolutely love for all rule question subjects to be in the form [<deck>] - <card> - <additional keywords>.

Example: "[Legacy] - Superhuman Durability - interaction with Fortitude"

Want to find all of the questions about a deck, just search for "[Legacy]" and you'll get a quick list. Might require some kind of magic for questions that belong to multiple decks (or just extra single-post threads that link to the base topic).

The fact that the search capability here is less than ideal is not an excuse for laziness when creating and titling threads. I would argue that it only strengthens the argument for having sensibly titled threads, since that has to be our primary search method in many cases.

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
grysqrl:

The fact that the search capability here is less than ideal is not an excuse for laziness when creating and titling threads. I would argue that it only strengthens the argument for having sensibly titled threads, since that has to be our primary search method in many cases.

That puts the burden on us the public to invest extra effort in something we're doing for fun.  I know >G is a small company with very limited funds, so I'm not demanding that they improve their forum's functionality, but I do consider it to be their job, not ours; the responsibility should fall on them to deal with it as best they're able to, not to delegate tasks to their consumers, even if we're willing.  I come here and I toss off the question that's on top of my head; from then on, the ball is no longer in my court.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Edwin:
Silverleaf wrote:
I'm actually talking about the "scanning the list of thread titles" type of searching.
But how many do you want to scan?  If the thread I'm looking for isn't on the New Topics or Active Topics or maaaaybe page 1 of Rules and Gameplay, I lack the patience to keep looking.  But if it's a thread I created for rules questions I myself asked, I can always find it in my Created Topics.  It'd be even better if there was a Subscribed Topics function, of course, so I could find threads others have created.  But the more different threads there are, the fewer of them fit in one list, so the more lists you have to look through to find them, and I'm not going to sit around going through page after page of lists trying to find something.

Sure, you can find it in your created topics. But what about everyone else? You want us to search through pages and pages each of many different threads (assuming we all have our own thread like you) to find a question, having to actually read every post? How is it reasonable to look under "Edwin" to find out what order Friction should play cards in?

You want everyone else to display far more patience than you're capable of displaying.

Edwin:
Quote:
More than likely a new person faced with this will just create a new thread to redundantly ask their question that has already been thoroughly answered and discussed elsewhere, which basically wastes everyone's time.
That much we agree on at least.  But that's not really a solvable problem, not unless >G will write a real rulebook for the game

Even games with the best written rulebooks generate questions, and we need a place to discuss them. A place that's organised sensibly so we can find things. Redundant questions here are the result of a person either not bothering to read the forum, or being unable to find what they're looking for. Better organisation leads to less redundancy with that last scenario.
